concept: JVM, JRE aur JDK ko teen nested layers ki tarah samjho. JVM actual bytecode execute karti hai. JRE JVM + runtime libraries provide karta hai. JDK development toolkit hai jisme compiler (`javac`) aur development tools ke saath runtime capabilities bhi hoti hain.

Developer ko code likhne aur compile karne ke liye JDK chahiye. End-user ko historically sirf runtime chahiye hota tha, lekin modern Java distributions me packaging model thoda different ho sakta hai. Learning ke liye core relationship yaad rakho: JDK is for development, JVM executes bytecode.
Platform independence ka matlab ye nahi ki JVM same binary har OS par hoti hai. JVM implementation OS-specific hoti hai, lekin tumhara bytecode portable ho sakta hai.

`java CalculatorApp` JVM launch karke bytecode execute karta hai.

interview: JDK, JRE, JVM difference?
JDK development tools provide karta hai; JRE runtime environment; JVM bytecode execute karti hai.
Java platform independent kaise?
Compiler portable bytecode generate karta hai; target OS par suitable JVM us bytecode ko execute karti hai.
JVM kya source code directly run karti hai?
Normally nahi. Java source pehle bytecode me compile hota hai, phir JVM execute karti hai.

concept: Identifier kisi class, variable, method, package, etc. ka programmer-defined naam hota hai. Example: `totalPrice`, `LoginPage`, `calculateTax`.

Rules: identifier digit se start nahi ho sakta, spaces allowed nahi, Java keyword use nahi kar sakte, aur `$`/`_` technically allowed hain lekin normal naming me avoid karna better hota hai. Java case-sensitive hai: `count` aur `Count` different hain.
Naming conventions readability ke liye important hain: classes PascalCase, methods/variables camelCase, constants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.

concept: Har primitive ka corresponding wrapper class hota hai: int→Integer, long→Long, double→Double, boolean→Boolean, char→Character. Wrapper object form provide karta hai.

concept: Operators values par operation karte hain. Important groups: arithmetic (`+ - * / %`), comparison (`== != > < >= <=`), logical (`&& || !`), assignment (`= += -=`), increment/decrement (`++ --`).

Comparison ka result boolean hota hai. Logical operators multiple conditions combine karte hain. `&&` aur `||` short-circuit karte hain: agar result pehle part se decide ho gaya to second part evaluate nahi hota.
Strings compare karne ke liye `==` nahi, usually `equals()` use karte hain; iska dedicated lesson Strings section me hai.

notes: Arrays Introduction
int[] a = {2,4} has two slots. a.length is 2. Reading a[2] throws an exception because its last index is 1.
Multi-Dimensional Arrays
int[][] grid = {{1,2},{3,4}} has two rows. grid[1][0] is 3. The outer array stores row references; a shallow outer copy still shares its rows.
Jagged Arrays
Rows can have different lengths: {{1},{2,3}}. Loop using each row's length, not the first row's size.
Arrays Utility Class
Arrays.sort mutates its input; copyOf creates a new array. equals compares one-dimensional contents; deepEquals compares nested contents. Sort a copy to preserve original order.
Final Arrays
final fixes the reference, not its elements. final int[] a = {1} still permits a[0] = 2. Defensive copies protect internal data from callers.

lessons.topic: Exceptions: fail clearly and clean up
concept: Exception normal flow interrupt karke failure signal karti hai. Catch wahi karo jahan recover, translate ya report kar sakte ho. Empty catch broken test ko green kar sakta hai.
Checked exceptions catch ya throws declaration demand karti hain. RuntimeException unchecked hai. AutoCloseable resources ko try-with-resources se deterministic cleanup do.
notes: Exception Basics
Exceptions include a type, message and stack trace. Checked exceptions require handling/declaration; unchecked exceptions often represent invalid arguments or state.
try/catch
Catch specific types before general ones. Keep try narrowly scoped. Execution continues after catch, not at the failing statement.
finally
finally normally runs even during return or exception propagation. Returning from finally can suppress failures, so avoid it. Abrupt JVM termination may prevent cleanup.
throw vs throws
throw raises an exception now; throws in a signature declares a possible checked failure to callers.
Custom Exceptions
Use a domain exception when callers must distinguish a meaningful failure. Keep the cause when translating an infrastructure exception.
Chained Exceptions
new IllegalStateException("Load failed", cause) preserves diagnostic context. Using only cause.getMessage() loses the original stack.
NullPointerException
Dereferencing null, including unboxing a null Integer, causes NPE. Validate required boundaries and represent optional absence deliberately.
Exceptions with Method Overriding
An override cannot add broader checked exceptions than the parent contract. It may narrow or omit them. Unchecked exceptions are not restricted that way.

lessons.topic: JVM memory: references, lifetime and leaks
concept: Variable aur object same nahi hain. Reference copy se new object nahi banta. Two references same mutable object dekh sakte hain, causing test contamination.
Garbage collector unreachable objects reclaim karta hai. Exact collection timing assume mat karo. Reachable but useless objects, jaise unbounded static cache entries, memory leak create karte hain.
notes: Memory Management
JVM manages allocation and reclamation. Application code still owns reachability and resource cleanup. Close sockets/files explicitly rather than waiting for GC.
Objects in Memory
Assigning a reference makes an alias. Clearing one reference leaves others intact. Java passes values, including copies of reference values.
JVM Memory Areas
Threads have execution stacks. Objects conceptually live on heap; class metadata uses areas such as HotSpot Metaspace. JIT can optimize physical allocation.
Stack vs Heap
Frames hold method call state and locals. References may be inside frames or objects. Deep recursion can cause StackOverflowError.
Garbage Collection
Unreachable objects are collectible, not necessarily immediately collected. System.gc is a request. Correctness must not depend on finalization.
Garbage Collectors
Collectors trade throughput, pause latency and memory use. Choose a supported collector based on measured workload, not universal rankings.
Memory Leaks
Static collections, unbounded caches and forgotten listeners retain objects. Diagnose retained paths and allocation patterns. Rising heap alone does not prove a leak.

notes: Collections Class
Collections is a utility class with operations such as sort and unmodifiableList. An unmodifiable view blocks mutation through that view but may reflect changes made to its underlying list.
Collection Interface
Collection is the root for List, Set and Queue. Map is separate because it represents key/value associations. Program to the smallest useful interface.
List
List preserves sequence and permits duplicates. ArrayList offers fast indexed reads; middle insertion shifts elements. LinkedList is not automatically faster for normal list use.
Set
Set enforces uniqueness under its equality contract. HashSet does not guarantee iteration order; LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order; TreeSet uses ordering comparison.
Queue
Queue represents pending work. offer adds, poll removes or returns null, peek inspects. ArrayDeque supports queues/stacks and rejects null.
Map
A Map associates unique keys with values. HashMap is unordered; LinkedHashMap preserves a defined iteration order. get returning null may mean absent or mapped-to-null.
Iterator
Iterator traverses elements. Remove through iterator.remove when supported. Structural changes outside iteration can raise ConcurrentModificationException; it is not a concurrency safety mechanism.
Comparable
Comparable defines natural ordering via compareTo. Return negative, zero or positive; avoid subtraction comparisons that may overflow.
Comparator
Comparator supplies external ordering. comparing and thenComparing combine rules without changing the class. Comparator equality affects sorted sets/maps.
HashMap Internals

HashMap hashes a key to a bucket and resolves collisions with equality checks. Resizing redistributes entries. Average lookup can be constant-time under good distribution; do not depend on iteration order.
equals() & hashCode()
Equal objects must have equal hash codes; unequal objects can collide. Keep key equality stable while an object is in a hash collection.

filter items choose karta hai; map har item transform karta hai; reduce many values ko one result mein combine karta hai. Stream once consume hoti hai. Side effects avoid karo so reasoning predictable rahe.
notes: Lambda Expressions
name -> name.length() provides a functional interface implementation. Captured local variables must be final or effectively final. Lambda does not create a new meaning of this.
Predicate
Predicate returns boolean via test. Combine with and, or and negate. Example: amount -> amount > 0.
Consumer
Consumer accepts a value and returns nothing. forEach uses it; side effects in parallel pipelines need careful synchronization and are often best avoided.
Supplier
Supplier produces a value with no argument. Useful for lazy defaults and fresh fixtures. A supplier may return the same or a new object depending on its implementation.
Method References
String::length refers to existing behaviour in concise syntax. It works only when its parameter/return shape matches the functional interface.
Streams
stream creates a lazy pipeline; collect, count or reduce trigger processing. Streams are single-use. Do not mutate their source during traversal.
map/filter/reduce
filter selects, map transforms, reduce combines with an associative operation and identity. mapToInt(...).sum avoids boxing for integer totals.
Collectors
Collectors.toList gathers results; groupingBy builds grouped maps. Do not assume the concrete collection returned by a collector. Java 16+ Stream.toList returns an unmodifiable list.
Optional
Optional represents possible absence. Prefer map/orElseGet/orElseThrow over unchecked get. orElse evaluates its argument eagerly; orElseGet invokes its supplier only when empty.

concept: Date/time API immutable types provide karti hai. LocalDate calendar date hai without time zone. Instant timeline par moment hai. Oslo user ka local time aur UTC timestamp same representation nahi hain.

notes: Date/Time Introduction
Choose a type matching meaning. Use Instant for timestamps, LocalDate for date-only values, ZonedDateTime for a local calendar representation in a named zone.
LocalDate
LocalDate.of(2026,9,27) represents a date without a time or offset. plusDays creates a new date; the old date stays unchanged.
LocalTime
LocalTime stores time-of-day without a date or zone. 09:00 alone cannot identify a unique instant.
LocalDateTime
LocalDateTime combines date and time without a zone. DST can make a local time ambiguous or nonexistent when mapped to a real zone.
Duration
Duration measures time-based amounts, such as elapsed seconds between Instants. A local calendar day is not always 24 elapsed hours across daylight-saving transitions.
Period
Period is calendar-based years, months and days. Use it for date arithmetic, not precise elapsed seconds.
DateTimeFormatter
DateTimeFormatter is immutable and thread-safe. ISO formatters avoid ambiguous day/month order. Match your pattern to the intended type and use strict parsing where needed.

lessons.topic: Concurrency: tasks, shared state and waiting
concept: Thread independent execution flow hai. Concurrency correctness ka hard part shared mutable state hai. count++ ek atomic operation nahi: read, add, write sequence hai.
Prefer independent tasks and immutable data. Shared state required ho to appropriate synchronization ya atomic types choose karo. Sleeps correct coordination ka substitute nahi hain.
notes: Threads Introduction
Threads share process memory but have separate call stacks. Timing and execution order are nondeterministic unless explicitly coordinated.
start() vs run()
start schedules a new thread which executes run. Calling run directly is a normal call on the current thread. A Thread instance can be started only once.
Main Thread
main runs on a thread. Wait for required work with join or Future.get. Non-daemon threads can keep the JVM alive.
Thread Priority
Priority is a scheduler hint, not an ordering or fairness guarantee. Tests must never depend on it.
Synchronization
synchronized locks a monitor and establishes visibility through its memory-ordering guarantees. All access to protected state must follow the same locking discipline.
Thread Safety
AtomicInteger incrementAndGet is atomic; ordinary int++ is not. Thread-safe individual operations do not necessarily make a multi-step business transaction atomic.
Locks
Explicit locks provide features such as timed acquisition. Always release in finally after successful acquisition. Locks do not help when other code ignores them.
ReentrantLock
A thread can reacquire a lock it already owns. Pair every lock() with unlock() in finally; avoid holding locks during slow external I/O.
Deadlock
Two tasks each waiting for the other's lock can never proceed. Use a consistent lock order, short critical sections and bounded waits.
Thread Pools
Executors reuse threads and queue tasks. Bound workloads and close executors. Fixed thread pools use an unbounded queue by default, so submission still needs control.
CompletableFuture
Compose async results with thenApply/thenCompose and combine independent work. Handle exceptional completion and timeouts. Blocking join inside the wrong executor can cause starvation.

lessons.topic: Files: paths, text and resource ownership
concept: File path file ka naam/location hai, open resource nahi. Reading small text file aur streaming huge file different choices hain. Charset explicitly set karna portable behaviour deta hai.
Buffered IO many small operations ka overhead reduce karta hai. Streams/readers close karna necessary hai; try-with-resources exceptions ke case mein bhi cleanup karta hai.
notes: Java IO
Byte streams process raw bytes; Readers/Writers process characters with an encoding. Binary data ko text reader se process mat karo.
Reader
Reader decodes characters. InputStreamReader bridges bytes to characters. Always know the charset instead of assuming the machine default.
Writer
Writer encodes characters. BufferedWriter batches writes. Flush pushes buffered data toward its destination; close also releases the resource.
File Handling
Path describes a location and Files performs operations. Use temporary directories for tests, handle absent files deliberately, and clean up test-owned files.
BufferedReader
BufferedReader reads text efficiently and provides readLine. A null result means end-of-file, not an empty line.
BufferedWriter
BufferedWriter writes text efficiently. Use newLine for the platform line separator when that matches your file contract.
NIO Basics
Files.readString/writeString are convenient for small files. Files.lines returns a stream that must be closed. Do not load unbounded files into memory.

lessons.topic: JDBC: SQL, transactions and connection ownership
concept: JDBC Java aur relational database ke beech standard API hai. Driver specific database se communicate karta hai. Connection transaction/session context deta hai; PreparedStatement parameters bind karta hai.
SQL text mein user input concatenate mat karo. Prepared statements data ko query structure se separate karte hain. Multi-step change ko transaction mein rakho so partial update persist na ho.
notes: JDBC Introduction
JDBC exposes interfaces for connections, SQL execution and results. A database driver implementation must be present at runtime.
JDBC Drivers
Use the driver for the target database/version. DriverManager selects drivers by JDBC URL; application pools commonly expose a DataSource.
Connection
A Connection holds transaction state. Use try-with-resources and acquire it for a bounded operation. Closing a pooled connection usually returns it to the pool.
Statement vs PreparedStatement
PreparedStatement binds values using ? placeholders. Parameters cannot replace identifiers such as table names; validate allowed identifiers separately.

lessons.topic: Testing and builds: choose the smallest useful boundary
concept: Test boundary pehle decide karo. Unit test one object ka behaviour isolate karta hai. Component test one deployable component ko meaningful boundary par exercise karta hai, often real internal layers with controlled external dependencies.

UI aur backend different components ho sakte hain. UI component test user interactions aur rendering cover kare; backend component test API/service/database behaviour. Dono ko few end-to-end tests connect karein, har scenario ko E2E banane ki zaroorat nahi.
notes: Maven

pom.xml declares dependencies and build plugins. src/main/java holds application code; src/test/java tests. mvn test runs unit tests; integration test phases require appropriate plugin configuration such as Failsafe.
JUnit 5
Tests express arrange, act, assert. Use parameterized cases for meaningful input boundaries. assertThrows checks expected failures; assertions should verify behaviour, not implementation wiring.
Mockito
Mocks replace collaborators; stubs specify responses and verify checks interactions. Avoid mocking the object under test. A service using a fake dependency may need no Spring context.
REST Assured
REST Assured drives HTTP APIs and asserts status/body. Configure base URI explicitly. It needs a running service or supported integration setup; it is not a Java compiler or database emulator.
TestNG
TestNG supplies test annotations, groups, data providers and lifecycle support. Do not mix JUnit and TestNG assumptions about runners/lifecycle in one test without explicit configuration.
Component Testing

Choose and document the component boundary. A backend component may include controller, service, repository and DB while stubbing outside services. A UI component can be mounted with its API boundary mocked.
Contract Testing
Contract tests verify consumer/provider compatibility at the boundary: method, path, schema and meaningful states. Stubs alone are not contract verification unless checked against the provider.
Testcontainers

Testcontainers starts real disposable dependencies through Docker, such as PostgreSQL. This is a real DB in a container, not a fake in-memory DB. Use realistic DB engines for vendor-specific behaviour.

lessons.topic: Spring Core: let the container wire objects
concept: Dependency Injection ka basic idea: object apni dependency khud create nahi karta; caller provide karta hai. Isse responsibility clear aur test setup simple hota hai. Framework ke bina constructor injection samajhna first step hai.

Spring ApplicationContext bean objects create, wire aur manage karta hai. @Component families scanned types register karti hain; @Bean methods explicit factory configuration provide karte hain. Boot is container setup ko convenient banata hai.
notes: Spring Introduction
Spring provides infrastructure such as dependency injection, transactions and web integration. It does not remove the need to understand Java object lifetimes.
IoC
Inversion of Control means framework controls object construction and lifecycle instead of application code manually managing every collaborator.
Dependency Injection

Constructor injection makes required collaborators explicit and supports final fields. With one constructor Spring can inject it without @Autowired. Multiple matching beans need a qualifier or primary choice.
Bean Lifecycle
Container instantiates, injects and applies lifecycle processing before a bean is used. Use lifecycle hooks for owned resources; avoid starting expensive work in arbitrary constructors.
Scopes

Singleton is one instance per bean definition per container, not one globally in the JVM. Prototype creates instances on lookup/injection; injecting prototype once into singleton does not create one per method call.
Configuration
@Configuration and @Bean register explicit factories. Component scanning discovers annotated types. Keep application root package above components; otherwise scanning may miss them.
Profiles
@Profile and configuration profiles select environment-specific beans/properties. Profiles are not a secrets store. Keep production credentials outside source control.

concept: Spring Boot ko Spring Framework ke upar bana hua accelerator samjho. Spring ka main idea hai objects ko loosely coupled banana aur unki dependencies Spring container se manage karwana. Spring Boot us setup ko fast banata hai: starter dependencies, auto-configuration, embedded server aur sensible defaults deta hai.

Simple language me: normal Java app me tum manually object bana sakte ho (`new Service()`). Spring app me container objects (beans) manage karta hai. Spring Boot me tum mostly business code likhte ho; framework bahut saari plumbing automatically configure kar deta hai.

`@SpringBootApplication` teen important ideas combine karta hai: configuration, auto-configuration aur component scanning. Application start hote hi Spring same package aur sub-packages me `@RestController`, `@Service`, `@Repository`, `@Component` jaise classes scan karke beans banata hai.

Typical request flow: Client/Postman/Test → Controller → Service → Repository → Database. First lesson me repository/database intentionally skip kar rahe hain. Pehle Controller + Service + Dependency Injection clear karenge.
Spring Boot ka goal magic yaad karna nahi hai. Request kis class me aayi, dependency kaun inject kar raha hai, business logic kahan hai, aur response kaise bana—ye flow samajhna sabse important hai.

interview: Spring aur Spring Boot me difference?
Spring core framework DI, IoC, MVC etc. provide karta hai. Spring Boot Spring ko opinionated defaults, auto-configuration, starters aur embedded server ke saath fast setup karta hai.
`@SpringBootApplication` kya karta hai?
Commonly configuration + component scanning + auto-configuration enable karta hai.
Bean kya hai?
Aisa object jiska lifecycle Spring container manage karta hai.
Dependency Injection kya hai?
Class apni dependency khud `new` karke create nahi karti; dependency outside/container se provide hoti hai.
`@RestController` vs `@Controller`?
`@RestController` REST responses ke liye convenient hai; return value default response body me jaati hai. `@Controller` commonly MVC views ke liye use hota hai.
Controller aur Service separate kyu?
HTTP concerns aur business logic separate rehte hain; code easier to test, reuse aur maintain hota hai.
Embedded server ka meaning?
App ko separately external Tomcat me deploy karna necessary nahi; Boot app packaged server ke saath directly run ho sakti hai.
Constructor injection kyu preferred?
Dependencies explicit hoti hain, immutable fields possible hote hain aur unit testing easy hoti hai.
Auto-configuration kya hai?
Classpath, existing beans aur configuration dekhkar Spring Boot common infrastructure automatically configure karne ki koshish karta hai.
QA engineer ko Spring Boot kyu samajhna chahiye?
API flow, logs, layers, dependency injection, component tests, mocks, database interactions aur microservice failures diagnose karna much easier hota hai.

notes: Boot Project Structure
Use the full pom.xml from the preceding Boot Project Structure lesson. Put main application in com.example.lab above other classes. Main sources and tests belong in separate Maven folders.
REST Controller
@RestController returns response bodies. @GetMapping chooses method/path; @PathVariable reads a path segment and @RequestParam reads a query. DTOs define your JSON contract.
Service Layer
@Service holds application rules and orchestration. Constructor injection exposes dependencies. Keep HTTP-specific ResponseEntity handling in the controller when practical.
Validation

Add spring-boot-starter-validation for Jakarta Bean Validation. @Valid validates request DTOs; @NotBlank and @Positive express constraints. Also enforce business invariants inside your service boundary.
Exception Handling
Use @RestControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler to map known failures to consistent HTTP responses. Do not expose stack traces or map every failure to 200.
Configuration Properties
@ConfigurationProperties binds grouped typed settings. Register it using scanning or enable annotation; validate critical values. Environment-specific endpoints and secrets should not be hardcoded.
Actuator
Actuator exposes operational health/metrics. Add its starter deliberately and restrict sensitive endpoints. Liveness and readiness answer different operational questions.
Testing Spring Boot

Service tests can run without Spring. @WebMvcTest isolates MVC with dependencies supplied as test doubles. @SpringBootTest plus @AutoConfigureMockMvc verifies wiring and MVC in-process; RANDOM_PORT additionally exercises a real server.

lessons.topic: Spring Data: persistence, migrations and real databases
concept: Entity Java object aur database row ke mapping define karti hai. Repository persistence operations expose karta hai. JPA SQL ko remove nahi karta; generated queries, constraints aur transaction behaviour samajhna still important hai.

Schema ko versioned Flyway migrations se evolve karo. Local disposable database useful hai, par H2 ya PostgreSQL Oracle ke all behaviours reproduce nahi karte. Oracle-specific SQL ke liye compatible Oracle environment test karo.
notes: JPA Basics
JPA defines ORM contracts; Hibernate is a common implementation. Persistence context tracks managed entities. Accessing lazy state outside its context can fail.
Entities
@Entity marks persistent types; @Id identifies rows. Provide a protected/public no-arg constructor as required. Records are useful DTOs but are not standard mutable JPA entities.
Repositories
Spring Data repository interfaces can generate common queries. Derived query names must match mapped properties. Use pagination for unbounded datasets.
Relationships
@ManyToOne and @OneToMany express associations. Fetch strategy affects query count. Inspect for N+1 queries and avoid exposing entity graphs directly as API JSON.
Transactions
@Transactional commonly uses a proxy boundary. Self-invocation can bypass interception. Runtime exceptions normally trigger rollback; configure checked-exception rules deliberately.
Flyway
Versioned migrations apply schema changes in order and record history. Do not edit already-applied versioned migrations; add a new migration. Test upgrading from a realistic prior schema.
Oracle/PostgreSQL
Drivers, dialects, sequences, empty-string behaviour and SQL features differ. Use the target engine for vendor-sensitive tests; a fake DB is not proof of Oracle compatibility.
Pagination
Pageable controls page size and sort. Use a stable tie-breaker such as ID. Offset pagination can drift under concurrent writes; keyset pagination may suit large changing datasets.

notes: Microservice Basics
Split around meaningful business ownership and independent change needs. A modular monolith may be simpler until those needs justify distributed boundaries.
Service Boundaries
Own data and rules inside a boundary. Sharing one database schema across many services couples deployments and undermines independence.
REST Communication
Specify timeout budgets, status/error contracts and idempotency. A timed-out client cannot assume the server performed no work.
OpenFeign/WebClient
Feign provides declarative clients; WebClient provides reactive HTTP operations. Framework convenience does not remove timeouts, error mapping or connection limits.
Resilience4j
Circuit breakers stop repeated calls during failure; retries repeat operations; bulkheads limit concurrent damage. They solve different problems and require measured thresholds.
Config
Externalize environment settings and validate them at startup. Keep secrets out of logs and source. Configuration changes can affect behaviour as much as code changes.
Service Discovery
Discovery maps logical services to live instances. Kubernetes service DNS may already provide what your architecture needs; avoid redundant discovery layers.
API Gateway
Gateway handles edge routing and cross-cutting concerns. Keep domain business logic out of the gateway when possible.
Observability
Logs explain events, metrics show aggregate behaviour, traces connect requests. Attach correlation identifiers and avoid sensitive payload logging.
Distributed Tracing
Propagate trace context across HTTP and messaging. A single slow span can identify whether delay is in DB, network or application logic.
Contract Testing
Verify consumer expectations against provider implementations. Include error states and optional/required fields, not only happy-path examples.

concept: Kafka event log hai. Producer topic mein records append karta hai; consumers positions track karke read karte hain. Consumer group partitions divide karta hai so same group mein each partition one active consumer ko assigned hoti hai.
Delivery repeat ho sakti hai: business work complete hone ke baad offset commit fail ho jaye to record again process hoga. Idempotent consumer duplicate event se duplicate effect prevent karta hai.
notes: Kafka Basics
Topics consist of ordered partitions. Ordering is per partition, not global across a topic. Retention and compaction policies determine how records remain available.
Producer
Producer sends records with optional keys. A stable business key can route related events consistently. Check acknowledgements/errors rather than assuming send means persisted success.
Consumer
Consumer polls records and processes them. Long processing can affect group membership. Bound work and use proper shutdown.
Consumer Groups
Consumers in the same group share partitions. Different group IDs each get an independent consumption view. More consumers than partitions leaves some idle.
Offsets
Offsets identify positions in partitions. Commit the next position deliberately according to processing semantics. Committing before work risks loss; after work permits redelivery.
Retries
Retry transient failures with bounds/backoff. Decide whether preserving partition order matters. Infinite retry can block progress on poison records.
DLQ
A dead-letter topic stores records that cannot be processed after your policy. Include error/context metadata and an operational replay path; a DLQ is not automatic recovery.
Idempotency
Deduplicate by event/business ID with atomic persistence and the side effect in one boundary when possible. A producer's idempotence does not automatically deduplicate external DB effects.
Testing Kafka
Use a real broker container for serialization, keys and consumer behaviour. Test duplicate delivery, poison records, ordering constraints and restart/rebalance cases.

lessons.topic: Docker and CI: repeatable builds and quality gates
concept: Docker image packaged filesystem aur startup configuration hai. Container us image ka running instance hai. Isse runtime reproducible hota hai, lekin host kernel, CPU architecture aur external services still matter.

notes: Docker Basics
Image is an immutable template; container is a running instance with writable state. Persist deliberate data through volumes, not accidental container files.
Dockerfile
Use a maintained base image and deterministic copy paths. Build artifact before copying it. Run as a non-root user where practical and do not bake secrets into layers.
Docker Compose

Compose defines related services, networks and volumes for local environments. Container-to-container addresses use service names, not localhost. Readiness requires health checks or retry-aware startup.
Testcontainers
Tests own disposable dependencies and discover mapped host ports dynamically. Do not assume the database runs on host port 5432. Always release owned resources.
Jenkins/GitHub Actions
Pipeline should checkout, set up toolchain, build, test and publish reports/artifacts. Credentials belong in protected secrets. Pull-request code must not receive unnecessary production secrets.
Quality Gates

Gate on meaningful required checks, not only coverage percentage. Include test failures, formatting/static analysis where useful, and measured reliability. Quarantined tests need ownership and expiry.

lessons.topic: Spring AI: connect a model through a testable boundary
concept: AI model call remote dependency hai with latency, cost aur nondeterministic output. Spring AI common Java abstractions provide karta hai. Model useful suggestion de sakta hai; returned text automatically verified fact ya safe command nahi hai.

Pehle plain Java interface ke through model behaviour isolate karo. Phir adapter mein ChatClient integrate karo. Provider credentials server-side configuration mein rakho, frontend ya code repository mein nahi.
notes: Spring AI Introduction

Spring AI integrates model and vector-store capabilities in Spring applications. It is not a model itself. Choose compatible Spring Boot/Spring AI versions and provider starter from their official docs.
ChatClient
ChatClient builds a prompt request; call().content() requests a text response. Treat provider errors and empty output explicitly. The site itself does not call an AI provider.
Prompt Templates
Templates combine instructions with bounded variables. Keep untrusted retrieved content separate in meaning from system instructions. A template is not a security boundary.
Structured Output
Map model output to a schema/type and validate it. Schema conformance does not establish factual correctness. Handle missing fields, invalid enums and rejected generations.
Tool Calling
A model may request an application tool; the application decides what executes. Validate arguments, authorize actions and require confirmation for consequential writes.
Embeddings
Embeddings map text to vectors useful for similarity. They are not encrypted text or guaranteed meaning. Model/dimension compatibility matters when querying stored vectors.
Vector Stores
Vector stores index embeddings and metadata. Apply access filters during retrieval; a shared vector index must not bypass document permissions.
Advisors
Advisors add cross-cutting prompt/response behaviour such as memory or retrieval. Understand ordering and retained data. Avoid duplicate or conflicting context injection.
Observability
Measure latency, error rate, token usage and task quality. Avoid recording secrets or full sensitive prompts unnecessarily; observability needs a data policy.

lessons.topic: RAG, MCP and a grounded QA assistant
concept: RAG mein relevant source material retrieve karke model ko context diya jata hai. Flow: question → permission-aware retrieval → relevant evidence → answer with references. Retrieval wrong ho to fluent answer bhi wrong ho sakta hai.

MCP tools/resources expose karne ka protocol hai. RAG knowledge supply karta hai; tools actions ya data access supply karte hain. Dono interchangeable nahi hain. A QA assistant may retrieve requirements and then use authorized tools to inspect test results.

Safe useful QA flow: requirement se acceptance criteria extract karo, existing tests retrieve karo, gaps propose karo, draft code generate karo, isolated environment mein run karo, then human review. Untrusted repository text ko system instructions mat samjho.
notes: RAG Basics
Retrieve evidence before generation and cite the actual source. When evidence is missing, say so. RAG reduces some knowledge gaps but does not guarantee correctness.
Chunking
Split documents into coherent pieces retaining headings and source IDs. Tiny chunks lose context; huge chunks dilute relevance. Measure retrieval quality with representative questions.
Embeddings
Embed query and corpus with compatible models. Re-embedding may be needed after a model/dimension change. Semantic similarity does not imply permission or truth.
Retrieval
Combine metadata filters with semantic or keyword search. Evaluate whether the needed evidence appears in top-k results, not only whether an answer sounds plausible.
Grounding
Tie each claim to supplied evidence and version. Conflicting or obsolete requirements require explicit handling. Instruct the model to treat source content as data, not authority to execute actions.
MCP Basics
MCP standardizes interaction with tools/resources exposed by servers. An MCP client still needs authentication, consent and operation-level authorization.
MCP Tools
Tools have structured inputs/outputs and may have side effects. Validate arguments and constrain scope. Reading test results is different from merging a change or deploying.
AI Test Generation
Generate draft cases from acceptance criteria and existing test conventions. Compile and execute in isolation. Generated tests may assert wrong requirements or duplicate weak checks.
Failure Analysis
Collect logs, assertions, diffs and environment facts. Separate observed evidence from hypotheses; verify a suspected cause before modifying code.
Evaluation & Guardrails
Track retrieval recall, groundedness, useful test coverage and unsafe-action rate. Use adversarial cases, permission tests and regression sets. Guardrails need checks at execution boundaries.

slides.text: Split documents into coherent pieces retaining headings and source IDs. Tiny chunks lose context; huge chunks dilute relevance. Measure retrieval quality with representative questions.

slides.title: Embeddings
slides.text: Embed query and corpus with compatible models. Re-embedding may be needed after a model/dimension change. Semantic similarity does not imply permission or truth.

slides.title: Retrieval
slides.text: Combine metadata filters with semantic or keyword search. Evaluate whether the needed evidence appears in top-k results, not only whether an answer sounds plausible.

slides.title: Grounding
slides.text: Tie each claim to supplied evidence and version. Conflicting or obsolete requirements require explicit handling. Instruct the model to treat source content as data, not authority to execute actions.

slides.title: MCP Basics
slides.text: MCP standardizes interaction with tools/resources exposed by servers. An MCP client still needs authentication, consent and operation-level authorization.

slides.title: MCP Tools
slides.text: Tools have structured inputs/outputs and may have side effects. Validate arguments and constrain scope. Reading test results is different from merging a change or deploying.

slides.title: AI Test Generation
slides.text: Generate draft cases from acceptance criteria and existing test conventions. Compile and execute in isolation. Generated tests may assert wrong requirements or duplicate weak checks.

slides.title: Failure Analysis
slides.text: Collect logs, assertions, diffs and environment facts. Separate observed evidence from hypotheses; verify a suspected cause before modifying code.

slides.title: Evaluation & Guardrails
slides.text: Track retrieval recall, groundedness, useful test coverage and unsafe-action rate. Use adversarial cases, permission tests and regression sets. Guardrails need checks at execution boundaries.
